### Use

We use the present simple to talk about schedules and timetables:

The train to Chattogram leaves at 10.30 p.m.

The ceremony starts at 6.00. Guests take their seats by 5.30.

The TV serial about crimes and investigation ends next week.

We use the present continuous to talk about fixed, planned or organized actions in future:

We're having some guests for dinner tonight.

My cousins are coming to Bangladesh on holidays in December.

I'm catching the 7.30 flight to Jashore tomorrow.

### Activity 1

Put in the right form of verb (simple present or present continuous) in the blanks.

a. : My brother is a painter. He $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ (be) in Japan now.

: What $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ (do) there?

: He $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ (have) a solo exhibition in Tokyo.

: How long will he stay there?

: Well, the exhibition $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ (end) tomorrow, and he $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ (come) back next week.
